precepts.text: David asked Achish for a place in some town in the country, and Achish gave him Ziklag that day; wherefore Ziklag pertaineth unto the kings of Judah unto this day.
precepts.point: Notice how this connects to yesterday's reading in chapter 27. Achish had given David Ziklag, and David and his men had gone up and invaded the Amalekites and the other old inhabitants of the land, leaving neither man nor woman alive. Now the Amalekites came back and smote Ziklag the same way, taking David's wives and the families of his men while they were gone up with Achish.

note.label: 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag

precepts.why:
David asked Achish, “let them give me a place in some town in the country, that I may dwell there”, and “Achish gave him Ziklag that day: wherefore Ziklag pertaineth unto the kings of Judah unto this day.”

That is the Ziklag of chapter 30. Notice how this connects to the reading in chapter 27. While David and his men were away with Achish, “the Amalekites had invaded the south, and Ziklag, and smitten Ziklag, and burned it with fire”, and taken the women captive. Yet “they slew not any, either great or small, but carried them away.”

note.label: 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag

precepts.why:
“David and his men went up, and invaded the Geshurites, and the Gezrites, and the Amalekites: for those nations were of old the inhabitants of the land.” “And David smote the land, and left neither man nor woman alive.” This is the raid the Amalekites answered at Ziklag.

Now the Amalekites came back and smote Ziklag the same way, taking David's wives and the families of his men while they were gone up with Achish. David and his men found the city “burned with fire; and their wives, and their sons, and their daughters, were taken captives”, and they “lifted up their voice and wept, until they had no more power to weep.”

David's two wives were taken, “Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.” “David was greatly distressed; for the people spake of stoning him”, every man grieved for his sons and his daughters: “but David encouraged himself in the Lord his God.”

“I pray thee, bring me hither the ephod”: David says I need that ephod, I have to ask a question. “And David enquired at the Lord, saying, Shall I pursue after this troop?” “And he answered him, Pursue”: David needed that ephod to speak directly with the Most High.

points: While David and his men were away with Achish, the Amalekites invaded the south and Ziklag, smote Ziklag and burned it with fire, and carried the women captive; they slew not any, great or small, but carried them away. David and his men came to the city on the third day, found it burned, and their wives and sons and daughters taken captive; they lifted up their voice and wept until they had no more power to weep.

Notice how this connects to yesterday's reading in chapter 27. Achish had given David Ziklag, and David and his men had gone up and invaded the Amalekites and the other old inhabitants of the land, leaving neither man nor woman alive. Now the Amalekites came back and smote Ziklag the same way, taking David's wives and the families of his men while they were gone up with Achish.

note.label: 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag

points: David's two wives were taken, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite. David was greatly distressed, for the people spake of stoning him, because the soul of all the people was grieved, every man for his sons and his daughters; but David encouraged himself in the Lord his God.

note.label: 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag

points: David said to Abiathar the priest, Ahimelech's son, Bring hither the ephod, and David inquired at the Lord: shall I pursue after this troop? shall I overtake them? The answer came, Pursue: for thou shalt surely overtake them, and without fail recover all.
David sought the Lord first and asked whether this thing was so before he moved; the Lord said go down, and you will recover.

note.label: 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag

points: David went, he and the six hundred men that were with him, and came to the brook Besor, where those that were left behind stayed. David pursued with four hundred men, for two hundred abode behind, which were so faint that they could not go over the brook Besor.

note.label: 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag

points: They found an Egyptian in the field and brought him to David; they gave him bread, water, a piece of a cake of figs, and two clusters of raisins, and when he had eaten his spirit came again to him, for he had eaten no bread nor drunk any water three days and three nights.

A sidebar worth saying: this man was faint because he had gone without food three days and three nights. Some of our people are like that after fasting one day on the last Friday of the month; we have got to check our spirits.

note.label: 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag

points: He was a young man of Egypt, servant to an Amalekite, left behind because he fell sick three days before; his company had invaded the south of the Cherethites, the coast of Judah, and the south of Caleb, and burned Ziklag with fire. David asked, Canst thou bring me down to this company? He answered, Swear unto me by God that thou wilt neither kill me nor deliver me into the hands of my master, and I will bring thee down to this company.

note.label: 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag

points: When he had brought him down, behold, the Amalekites were spread abroad upon all the earth, eating and drinking and dancing because of all the great spoil they had taken out of the land of the Philistines and out of the land of Judah.

note.label: 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag

points: David smote them from the twilight even unto the evening of the next day, and there escaped not a man of them, save four hundred young men which rode upon camels and fled.

note.label: 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag

points: David recovered all that the Amalekites had carried away, and rescued his two wives; there was nothing lacking to them, neither small nor great, neither sons nor daughters, neither spoil nor any thing that they had taken. David took all the flocks and the herds, and they said, This is David's spoil.

note.label: 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag

points: When David came back to the two hundred men at the brook Besor, all the wicked men and men of Belial among those that went with David said, Because they went not with us, we will not give them ought of the spoil that we have recovered, save every man his wife and his children. Notice these were David's own men, yet the scripture calls them wicked men and men of Belial; David called that thinking of the devil, saying they had the devil on them for even thinking like that.

note.label: 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag

points: That is the same spirit a lot of our people have today: I went down there, my hands got me this, you have got to get your own. David said, Ye shall not do so, my brethren, with that which the Lord hath given us, who hath preserved us and delivered the company that came against us into our hand.

note.label: 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag

points: The ruling: as his part is that goeth down to the battle, so shall his part be that tarrieth by the stuff; they shall part alike. Those that went down into the battle split the spoil with those that stayed behind, and from that day forward David made it a statute and an ordinance for Israel unto this day.

note.label: 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag

points: When David came to Ziklag he sent of the spoil unto the elders of Judah, even to his friends, saying, Behold a present for you of the spoil of the enemies of the Lord.

The chapter in sum: the Amalekites spoiled the city and took the families while the men were gone up with Achish; David sought the Lord first, was told to pursue and recover, and went down and recovered all; and when his men that fought did not want to share with the men that were too faint, David made everybody part alike.

note.label: 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag

points: The spoil went to them in Bethel, in south Ramoth, in Jattir, in Aroer, in Siphmoth, in Eshtemoa, in Rachal, in the cities of the Jerahmeelites, in the cities of the Kenites, in Hormah, in Chorashan, in Athach, in Hebron, and to all the places where David himself and his men were wont to haunt.
